main_text.head: DE IGNE SUBTERRANEO.
main_text.p: 5. Ignes subterraneos esse probant flammæ illæ quæ eructantur in Sici-lia ad Ætnam montem, in regno Neapolitano ad montem Vesu-vium, & in Islandia ad montem Heclam.

6. Causa ejusmodi ignium creditur vulgò Sol: Verùm cum non appareat quomodo possit tam profundè in terram solis calor penetrare, qui vix ad pedes paucos superficiem calefacit, alia causa quærenda est.

7. Alii recurrunt ad ignem centralem, ideft in centro terræ existentem: Verum cum concipi non possit, quomodo ignis ille sit sine pabulo, & se perpetua quadam circulatione devoret, absque fumo & fuligine sit, interim autem perpetuò ardeat, calorémque suum quoquoversum in superficiem terræ diffundat, alia causa quærenda est.

8. Dici igitur potius debet, corpus Terræ esse quasi omniseminarium, ideft continere rerum omnium semina; ignis autem semina quæ sunt in terra sese præsertim prodere ob insignem mobilitatem, & cumulatiora facta in quibusdam regionibus evadere in flammas & incendia creare: Quoniam verò quæ[?] poteft, quibus præsertim corporibus semina ignis sint illigata, seu quæ corpora præsertim contineant illos spiritus igneos; dici-mus duos esse concretos succos præ cæteris pingues, scilicet sulphur ac bitumen: Ejusmodi autem spiritus & halitus incalescunt, quatenus corpuscula ignis ex quibus contexitur halitus, libera evadunt: Constat verò corpuscula nitri calorem seutentia facere, tum ad diffla-tionem; tum ad intensionem caloris: Cum sit autem notum, ex nitro intermisto sulphuri bitumini, & calci vivæ misturas quasdam fieri, quæ aspersione humidi, velut etiam sputo accendantur, quidni similes commistiones fieri sub terra valeant, quæ humore aqueo illatu incensiones fiant.

9. Hic quæri solet primò, quomodo ÆNea[?], Vesuviana, aliáque incendia tot jam perdurent sæculis? Respondetur, id esse quia terra illis locis maximè abundat sulphure ac bitumine, quæ sunt ignis præcipua fomenta. At quomodo illa semel accensa perpetuò non ardent, sed per intervalla duntaxat[?]? Respondetur, id esse quia dum flammæ rumpunt[?], locaque subver-ruit, collabuntur ruinæ ac veluti rudera, subtectcurrentes etiam aquæ-

page.notes: Printed page 165 with running head PHYSICÆ at top. The heading DE IGNE SVBTERRANEO is set in spaced capitals and is read as SUBTERRANEO with u/v corrected. Paragraph 5 opens with a large initial I joined to the italic word Ignes. The line ending "subver-" continues into "ruit," as printed. The word "tumpunt" is read as printed; it is probably a misprint for "rumpunt" and is marked [?]. "ÆNea" is hard to read and is marked [?]. "duntaxat" is uncertain. "quæ.i" after "Quoniam verò" is unclear and marked [?]. The final word "aquæ-" carries a dash at the line end which may be a printed hyphen; the text continues on the next page. Signature "X·3" is read as X 3. The printed ornament band between the paragraphs is not text and is omitted. Watermark or digitiser text at bottom right is omitted.
